title: Senior Manager- Forward Deployed Engineer
description: ENGINEER Location: Chennai (on site) | Type: Fulltime About Newpage Solutions Newpage Solutions is a global digital health innovation company helping people live longer, healthier lives. We partner with life sciences organisations which include, pharmaceutical, biotech and healthcare leaders, to build transformative AI and data driven technologies addressing real-world health challenges. From strategy and research to UX design and agile development, we deliver and validate impactful solutions using lean, human-centered practices. We are proud to be a ‘ Great Place to Work®’ certified company for the last three consecutive years. We also hold a top Glassdoor rating and are named among the "Top 50 Most Promising Healthcare Solution Providers" by CIOReview. As an organisation, we foster creativity, continuous learning and inclusivity, creating an environment where bold ideas thrive and make a measurable difference in people’s lives. Your Mission We are hiring a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer to take the hardest AI problems in Finance and Global Business Services from whiteboard to production for a global pharmaceutical company, and to set the patterns the rest of the team builds on. You will join a function team, define the problem, and lead the build from first prototype through production handoff and support, taking the engagements that span multiple systems or teams in areas such as financial close, forecasting, accounts receivable, procure-to-pay, tax, treasury and shared services operations. This is a senior hands-on individual contributor and technical lead role in the company's Finance and Global Business Services technology and AI capability center in Chennai. You will set the engineering patterns other Forward Deployed Engineers follow, review their designs and code, and still write code every week, alongside Product Owners, process owners, and digital platform and architecture teams. You will work directly with Finance and Global Business Services leaders worldwide, so you find out fast whether what you build works. You can grow your career through technical leadership without moving into people management. Success is measured by adoption, demonstrable business outcomes (time saved, quality, risk, controls, cycle time, better decisions, financial impact) and how much of your work others reuse. The role needs regular overlap with US and European time zones, including some early-evening IST calls, and can be demanding at times, including period-end close support and leading the response to production incidents. You don't need every bonus skill listed. If you have led AI into production that people use and want to work close to the business, we want to hear from you. What You’ll Do Problem Discovery and Business Partnership Work in person in Chennai while embedding virtually with assigned Finance and Global Business Services teams. Lead discovery for complex, cross-functional use cases through regular calls, screen-share walkthroughs and process reviews with senior stakeholders and process owners across regions, including the US and Europe, and shape them into roadmaps with measurable outcomes. Work with Product Owners to turn priorities and specifications into solution designs and delivery plans, and to rank use cases by value, feasibility and risk. Say no, or not yet, when a use case lacks data, sponsorship or a clear value case, and push back when a specification doesn't match the underlying problem or runs into technical issues and limitations. Technical Leadership and Build Serve as technical lead on complex engagements: own solution design, stay hands-on in the code, and lead the design of agentic AI built with frontier models on the company's enterprise AI platforms. Design multi-agent and multi-step workflows on Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI and other market-leading runtimes, using frameworks such as Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph and Lang Chain, with MCP, A2A and APIs connecting enterprise systems, deterministic business rules and human approval steps. Set coding standards, evaluation practice and quality bars for the engagements you lead, including review standards for AI-generated code. Use AI coding agents in your daily workflow to speed delivery, show other engineers how to use them well, and make build-versus-buy and platform choices with digital platform and architecture teams. Data and Enterprise Integration Lead integration across Finance and Global Business Services data and systems through governed MCP tools or APIs and certified data products, such as SAP S/4HANA, Snowflake (including Cortex), Databricks, SAP Ariba and Business Network, Oracle EPM, Microsoft 365, other enterprise platforms and custom solutions. Help shape a shared Finance and Global Business Services data and AI foundation (ontology, rules engine, MCP tool library and decision ledger), and decide which patterns become shared building blocks. Define data contracts, semantic models and access patterns, and extend the shared ontology and business rules, such as Delegation of Authority, Segregation of Duties and materiality, that other engineers and agents reuse. Set data access, entitlement and classification practice for financial and personal data on the engagements you lead. Controls, Compliance and Responsible AI Own control design for your solutions. Engage SOX, Internal Audit, Privacy, Legal, Security and AI governance early, including data privacy (GDPR, India DPDP Act) and EU AI Act review, and pass required gates before release. Define evaluation and monitoring for accuracy, drift and failure modes on financial outputs, and make sure agent evidence, approvals and actions are recorded in the decision ledger. Enforce responsible AI safeguards: data access controls, prompt injection defenses, human review and output monitoring. Production, Reliability and Reuse Own production readiness and ongoing support for the solutions you lead: LLMOps practice, deployment pipelines, monitoring, incident response and run costs. Establish support ownership, runbooks, service expectations, escalation paths, knowledge transfer and root cause analysis for production solutions. Set the standard for logging, tracing, monitoring and alerting with Azure Monitor, Application Insights and Foundry Observability. Convert proven solutions into reusable components, templates and accelerators across Finance and Global Business Services, and identify and pay down technical debt before it blocks scale. Mentoring, Value and Adoption Mentor Manager-level Forward Deployed Engineers, and engineers in Finance and Global Business Services function teams, through design reviews, pairing and code review. Contribute to Forward Deployed Engineering playbooks, interview loops and team upskilling. Build business cases and track realized value: hours saved, cycle time, cost avoidance and risk reduction. Present results and tradeoffs to senior Finance and Global Business Services stakeholders and Forward Deployed Engineering leadership, and build champions in the business so adoption sticks. What You Bring Engineering and AI Delivery 7+ years of software or data engineering experience, including at least three years building and shipping LLM-based applications to production, with at least one multi-step agentic system with tool use, evaluation and monitoring. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science or a related field. Technical lead experience on complex, multi-system builds. Expert-level Python, with strong TypeScript/JavaScript and SQL. Hands-on experience with cloud architecture, ideally Azure; AWS is also considered. Includes API-first design, CI/CD and observability. Hands-on LLMOps practice: evaluation, tracing, and prompt, model and agent versioning. Daily use of AI coding agents in your own engineering work, with the judgement to review AI-generated code. Business Partnership and Leadership Able to partner with the business, turn messy problems into working solutions, and show the impact in numbers. Proven ability to influence senior business stakeholders without formal authority. Experience mentoring engineers. Preferred Qualifications A Master's degree in a technical field, or a finance or accounting background combined with engineering experience. Deep knowledge of finance processes such as record-to-report, order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, FP&A or treasury, or prior work in finance technology. Experience integrating with SAP (S/4HANA, GTS, Ariba), Snowflake (including Cortex), Databricks, the Azure AI stack (AI Foundry, AI Search, Document Intelligence, Azure ML), Vertex AI or Oracle EPM; comparable enterprise platforms are also considered. Experience with agent orchestration frameworks such as Microsoft Agent Framework, Lang Graph or Lang Chain, MCP server development and A2A; other orchestration frameworks are also considered. Experience with ontologies, knowledge graphs or rules engines. Experience with SOX and IT general controls in a regulated industry. Experience turning bespoke solutions into reusable platforms or products. AWS or Azure Solutions Architect or Developer certification, or the equivalent on other market-leading platforms. What We Offer At Newpage, we’re building a company that works smart and grows with agility, where driven individuals come together to do work that matters. We offer: A people-first culture - Supportive peers, open communication and a strong sense of belonging Smart, purposeful collaboration - Work with talented colleagues to create technologies that solve meaningful business challenges Balance that lasts - We respect your time and support a healthy integration of work and life Room to grow - Opportunities for learning, leadership and career development, shaped around you Meaningful rewards - Competitive compensation that recognises both contribution and potential Ready to Apply? Let’s build the future of health together. Apply below or reach out to: Ramadevi.bhumireddy@newpage.io More about Newpage Newpage is a digital health solutions company. We devote ourselves to advancing the quality of life by enhancing health and optimizing the longevity of people. We do this by, passionately building futuristic technologies for global organizations across the healthcare ecosystem. We partake at every stage from problem definition, strategy & service design, user research, UX design, and agile software development – utilizing lean practices to deliver and validate highly innovative digital health solutions that drive user value and business transformation. description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language , enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover
